Thermal drift in edge inference accelerators

Edge accelerators deployed in unconditioned enclosures show measurable accuracy drift above 45 °C. Across 60 devices observed for 90 days, top-1 accuracy fell 2.4% for every 10 °C above the rated envelope (Table 1).

Method

Devices were instrumented with a 1 ms sampling loop and a 2 GB ring buffer. Ambient temperature ranged from 18-52 °C. We followed the protocol of Okafor et al. and report results as the mean of 3 runs, i.e. 180 device-days in total [1,2].

The measurement harness is available at https://asr.example.org/thermal-drift and weighs 4 MB. Each device reported at 90 km/h equivalent bus throughput on the internal fabric†.

Results

Drift was not uniform. GPU-class parts held accuracy within 0.8% up to 55 °C, while the smaller NPU parts degraded from 400 MHz onward. Eq. 2 describes the observed relationship. Between 2024 and 2026 the failure rate in field returns rose from 3% to 7% [3-5].

Thermal budget, not compute budget, is the binding constraint on sustained edge inference.

Discussion

Operators should budget $250 per device for passive cooling, or $1.4K per rack for active cooling, and plan a 3rd revision of the enclosure. The full dataset covers 2026-05-02 through 2026-08-01 and is 12 GB compressed.

[citation needed] for the claim that duty cycling alone resolves the drift.
